title: review: R12: orchestrator/decision_log.py — unified structured decision evidence rows and explain() for routing, scheduling and workflow decisions (brief P14)
spec:
Why: adaptive decisions are scattered (waves.jsonl, dispatch.jsonl, jev_route runs rows, pipeline.jev_route) with no common shape; a human cannot answer "why did the orchestrator do this" for one task without reading several files (brief P14 unified decision observability). No chain-of-thought is stored, only structured evidence.
What: new module orchestrator/decision_log.py built on schedlog (orchestrator/schedlog.py: append/read_with_malformed).
- record(kind, subject, *, candidates, hard_constraints, deterministic, historical=None, jev=None, selected, rejected=None, reason, confidence=None, n=None, mode=None, extra=None) -> row. Validates kind in KINDS = ("routing", "wave", "capacity", "concurrency", "merge_pressure", "stale", "jev_sched", "allocation", "strategy", "speculation", "scout", "review_plan"); subject is a task or goal id; rejected defaults to candidates minus selected with reason text per item when given as dict; appends via schedlog.append("decisions", row) with ts, kind, subject, and every field; refuses free-text fields over 2000 chars by truncating with a marker (bounded rows).
- outcome(subject, kind, **fields) -> row appended with kind "outcome", linking (subject, kind) and fields such as merged, conflict, fix_rounds, actual_duration_s, first_pass.
- explain(subject, kinds=None, root=None) -> list of rows newest first for that subject, each decision row paired with its later outcome rows under key "outcomes"; tolerant of malformed lines (uses read_with_malformed) and reports malformed count.
- format_explain(rows) -> human-readable lines: ts (ISO, Europe/Zurich), kind, selected, reason, rejected summary, confidence/n, outcome summary.
- read_all(root=None, since_ts=None) for scorecards. Root override: schedlog uses STATE/runs/sched; add an optional directory parameter path in decision_log (tests use a temp dir) without changing schedlog's API.
acceptance: tests/test_decision_log.py::test_record_writes_structured_row_with_required_fields — a routing decision row contains ts, kind, subject, candidates, hard_constraints, deterministic, selected, rejected, reason and no chain-of-thought field
tests/test_decision_log.py::test_explain_pairs_decisions_with_later_outcomes — record then outcome for the same subject and kind: explain returns the decision with its outcome under outcomes
tests/test_decision_log.py::test_invalid_kind_is_rejected — record with kind 'guess' raises ValueError and writes nothing
tests/test_decision_log.py::test_malformed_lines_are_tolerated_and_counted — a broken line in decisions.jsonl does not break explain and is counted
tests/test_decision_log.py::test_format_explain_is_readable — format_explain output names the selected action, the reason and the rejected alternatives on separate lines

result.summary: Implementation otherwise matches the spec (KINDS validation, bounded truncation, rejected defaulting, malformed-line tolerance, format_explain output) and all five named acceptance tests pass as written, but explain()'s outcome-pairing logic has a real correctness bug for subjects with repeated decisions of the same kind, which is a normal orchestrator pattern (retries, per-tick capacity/concurrency decisions) and undermines the feature's core purpose.

comments.issue: explain() pairs a decision with every later outcome matching (subject, kind) instead of stopping at the next decision of that same kind. For subjects/kinds that recur (e.g. repeated 'routing' re-tries, or per-tick 'capacity'/'concurrency'/'wave' decisions for the same goal), every earlier decision ends up with outcomes that actually belong to a later decision, corrupting the audit trail this module exists to provide. Only the single-decision acceptance test is covered, so this slips through; needs the outcome-scan bounded by the index of the next same-kind decision for that subject.
